hints: Establish a positive direction for motion along the horizontal line, such as taking the initial direction of P as positive.
Calculate the initial momentum of each particle using $p = mv$, assigning opposite signs to P and Q since they travel towards each other: $u_P = 0.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $u_Q = -1\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Apply the principle of conservation of linear momentum: the total initial momentum equals the total final momentum, noting that Q comes to rest ($v_Q = 0$).
Solve the linear equation for $v_P$. Remember that speed is the magnitude of velocity, so state the final answer as a positive quantity.
walkthrough:
Name the principle of conservation of linear momentum. In the absence of external horizontal forces on the smooth plane, the total momentum before collision equals the total momentum after collision:
$$m_P u_P + m_Q u_Q = m_P v_P + m_Q v_Q$$

Choose a sign convention: take the direction of the initial motion of $P$ to the right as positive. Identify each given quantity:
$$m_P = 0.2\text{ kg},\quad u_P = +0.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$m_Q = 0.3\text{ kg},\quad u_Q = -1\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Because $Q$ comes to rest after the collision, its final velocity is:
$$v_Q = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Substitute all known numerical values into the conservation of momentum equation:
$$(0.2)(0.5) + (0.3)(-1) = (0.2)v_P + (0.3)(0)$$
Carry out the multiplications on the left-hand side:
$$0.10 - 0.30 = 0.2v_P + 0$$
$$-0.20 = 0.2v_P$$

Divide both sides by $0.2$ to solve for the final velocity of $P$:
$$v_P = \frac{-0.20}{0.2} = -1\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The negative sign indicates that particle $P$ has reversed its direction of motion. Speed is the scalar magnitude of velocity, so:
$$\text{Speed of } P = 1\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
